32 SELLER’S STAMP DUTY
The seller must pay the prevailing stamp duties relating to the sale of the flat (including but
not limited to Seller’s Stamp Duty) as may be imposed by the Government from time to
time. Where the seller needs to pay part of such stamp duties in cash, the seller shall pay
to HDB upon HDB’s request after the acceptance of the resale application, within the
timeframe specified by HDB and in any mode of payment that HDB may decide, failing
which HDB reserves the right not to approve the resale.
33 REFUND OF CPF SAVINGS
33.1 Where the seller has used his CPF savings to pay for his flat, such CPF savings together
with interest calculated up to the resale completion date will have to be refunded to his CPF
account. The refund of CPF savings is subject to the CPF Board’s prevailing policies, rules,
regulations, terms and conditions.
33.2 If the sale proceeds are not enough to effect a full CPF refund, the seller shall, as may be
directed by HDB, pay the cash deposit received from the buyer (or any part thereof) to HDB
as part of the refund to his CPF account. HDB shall not be responsible or liable to any
party for any action, proceeding, claim, demand, liability, loss, charge, damage, cost and/or
expense which may be brought against, become payable by and/or incurred by any party
arising from or in relation to the parties’ failure to complete the resale transaction due to
the seller’s failure to comply with HDB’s directions to pay the deposit (or any part thereof)
to HDB.
34 PAYMENT OF CASH PROCEEDS
34.1 HDB will credit the cash proceeds of sale after the payouts for redemption of any
outstanding housing loan, CPF refund and other deductibles (“cash proceeds”) to the
seller’s bank account electronically via an e-payment system (including but not limited to
HDB’s e-payment system or any other system used for the payment) (“e-Payment System”),
subject to the following:
a) The inherent risks of internet transaction/payment are such that transmissions may
be subject to interruption, interception, hacking, fluctuation, inaccuracy, defect,
corruption, loss, connection error, transmission blackout, delayed or failed
transmission and/or incorrect transmission. The seller agrees not to hold HDB liable
under any circumstances for any claim or demand (for damages, losses, expenses,
etc.) which he may have or be exposed to as a result of his assuming such risks.
b) While every care is taken by HDB in providing the e-Payment System, HDB does not
warrant that the e-Payment System will be provided uninterrupted or free from error
or that any identified defect will be corrected.
c) To the fullest extent permitted by law, HDB shall not be liable to the seller or any third
party for any loss, damage, expense or cost including but not limited to direct, indirect,
punitive, special, consequential or incidental damages, loss of income, revenue,
profits, business, business contracts or business opportunities, anticipated savings,
economic loss, which may result directly or indirectly from HDB effecting payment of
the cash proceeds due to the seller via the e-Payment System or any delay in
operation or transmission; or communication or system failure or malfunctions in the
system, equipment or software; or any errors, omissions, inaccuracy or
incompleteness arising from HDB effecting payment of the cash proceeds due to the
seller via the e-Payment System.

34.2 For the purpose of the e-payment and where the seller has appointed HDB to act as his
solicitor in the sale of the flat, the seller shall provide his bank account to receive the cash
proceeds when submitting the resale application. Unless otherwise specified by HDB, the
type of bank account to be provided will depend on the ownership, manner of holding and
circumstances for the sale of the flat as follows:
(a) The bank account must be from the 3 local banks, namely, DBS/POSB, OCBC and
UOB.
(b) If the flat is solely owned, the bank account must belong to the sole owner.
(c) If the flat is jointly owned and held in joint tenancy, the bank account must be held
jointly by all the owners of the flat.
(d) If the flat is jointly owned and held in tenancy-in-common, each individual owner of
the flat must provide a bank account belonging to each of them.
(e) If the flat is sold by an executor or administrator of the late flat owner’s estate, the
bank account must belong to the estate of the late owner.
(f) If the flat is sold pursuant to a Court Order following a divorce, each individual owner
of the flat must provide a bank account belonging to each of them.
(g) If the flat is sold by an Attorney acting under a Power of Attorney or a Donee acting
under a Lasting Power of Attorney given by a flat owner, or by a Deputy appointed
by the court, the bank account must belong to the payee stated in the Power of
Attorney or Lasting Power of Attorney or Court Order, where applicable.
(h) If the flat is sold by an owner who is an undischarged bankrupt and who forms part
of a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) household, this owner’s share of the cash
proceeds will be issued to the Official Assignee or a trustee in bankruptcy as
appointed by the court, where applicable. The remaining flat owner(s) must provide
the bank account(s) in accordance with clause 34.2 (a) to (g).
34.3 The seller is responsible for ensuring the correctness of the bank account, and the accuracy
and completeness of the bank account details provided to HDB and shall at all times
exempt and indemnify HDB from all actions, proceedings, claims, demands, costs and
liability whatsoever, which may be brought and incurred by HDB arising from any act matter
or thing that is performed under the seller’s direction(s) to credit the cash proceeds to the
bank account provided.
34.4 Any payments made by HDB to the seller, including the cash proceeds, will be credited
electronically to the bank account provided by the next working day after the resale
completion.

2 Words expressing the singular include the plural and vice versa.

CAUTION:
It is an offence for any person to give HDB false information relating to the sale or purchase of an
HDB flat. Any person who gives false information shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on
conviction to a fine not exceeding $5,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months or
to both.
HDB also reserves the right to debar any person who makes a false statement from buying a flat^,
taking over ownership of a flat^ by way of transfer, being included as a member of the core family
nucleus or an essential occupier of a flat^ or taking up an HDB housing loan for a period of 5 years
from the date of cancellation of the resale application or the date of approval to compulsorily acquire
the flat. Any existing application registered on the HDB’s rental waiting list will be cancelled. Any
existing Intent to Sell or HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) Letter will also be invalidated.
(^includes a flat under the Design, Build and Sell Scheme or a unit under the Executive Condominium
Housing Scheme)
HDB’S PRIVACY POLICY
HDB collects personal data from you to administer HDB's public housing programmes and services.
We may share necessary data with other Government agencies unless such sharing is prohibited
by legislation. This is to enable us to serve you in the most convenient, efficient and effective way.
We will NOT share your personal data with non-Government entities, except where such entities
have been authorised to carry out specific Government services.
If you would like to find out more about HDB’s Data Protection and Privacy Policy, you can visit our
